UK Inflation Rises to 3.6% Driven by Fuel and Tobacco Costs

UK inflation reached a 12-month high of 3.6% in the year to October, primarily due to increased prices for petrol, diesel, and tobacco. Official figures indicate that higher energy bills and a tobacco duty hike also contributed to the rise.
